verified: creep buckling = instability at finite critical time under constant load below instantaneous Euler load (Cambridge critical-time formulae; IJSS 1993 imperfection growth under constant end load)
mechanism: creep lowers effective critical load over time; initial imperfections grow via hereditary integrals; safe load limit exists below which process stabilizes (ASCE 1985)
Rabotnov-Shesterikov critical-load vs Hoff critical-time criteria are correlated (Acta Mechanica)

correspondence principle does not transfer to stability: Urbach-Efrati stationarity + transient acquired stability two-result theory (Science Advances / arXiv); FGM correspondence-principle failure (J Appl Mech 2003)
codes handle creep via load duration and service classes (Eurocode 5) rather than explicit creep buckling clauses
unverified: Laplace-plane pole-movement mechanism (transform inversion moves poles, stable transformed solution maps to unstable time-domain response) - consistent with retrieved theory but not stated in any retrieved source
clause-level creep buckling safety format text in EN 1995-1-1
